{{Nihongo|'''Kazuya Kato'''|加藤 和也|Katō Kazuya|born on January 17, 1952}}<ref name="PKK">{{Cite web |title=Achievements of Kazuya Kato |url=http://www.asiapacific-mathnews.com/04/0401/0013_0015.pdf |last=Saito |first=Shuji |date= |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=Asia Pacific Mathematics}}</ref> is a Japanese mathematician who works at the [[University of Chicago]], as a professor, and specializes in [[number theory]] and [[arithmetic geometry]]. He is a member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, elected in 2011. He received the 2005 Imperial Prize of the Japan Academy.<ref name="amacad">{{Cite web |title=Professor Kazuya Kato |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/kazuya-kato |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Kazuya Kato grew up in the prefecture of [[Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama]] in [[Japan]]. He attended college at the [[University of Tokyo]], from which he also obtained his master's degree in 1975, and a [[PhD]] in 1980.<ref name="PKK"/>

==Career==
Kato lectured, as a professor, at [[Tokyo University]] in 1982, then from 1997 to 2001. He also taught at [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]] in 1992. He later became a faculty member at the [[University of Chicago]] in 2009.<ref name="UChicago">{{Cite web |title=Faculty members receive named, distinguished service professorships |url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/faculty-members-receive-named-distinguished-service-professorships#Kazuya%20Kato |date=2011-07-06 |access-date=2026-07-12 |website=UChicago News - the University of Chicago}}</ref>

A special volume of ''[[Documenta Mathematica]]'' was published in honor of his 50th birthday, together with research papers written by leading number theorists and former students it contains Kato's song on Prime Numbers.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.mathematik.uni-bielefeld.de/documenta/vol-kato/vol-kato.html|editor1-first=Spencer |editor1-last=Bloch |editor1-link=Spencer Bloch |editor2-first=Ivan |editor2-last=Fesenko |editor2-link=Ivan Fesenko |editor3-first=Luc |editor3-last=Illusie |editor3-link=Luc Illusie |editor4-first=Masato |editor4-last=Kurihara |editor5-first=Shuji |editor5-last=Saito |editor6-first=Takeshi |editor6-last=Saito |editor7-first=Peter |editor7-last=Schneider |title=Extra Volume of Documenta Mathematica: Kazuya Kato's Fiftieth Birthday |year=2003 |publisher=Documenta Mathematica}}</ref>

==Research and contributions==
Kato has researched and contributed to various areas in number theory and geometry, some of which include: the "Galois theory of fields, Iwasawa theory, p-adic cohomology, L-functions, K-theory and Hodge theory." He started the use of logarithmic structure to redefine Hodge structure as well.<ref name="amacad"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 2005, Kato received the [[Imperial Prize of the Japan Academy]] for "Research on Arithmetic Geometry".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.japan-acad.go.jp/en/activities/jyusho/k-l.html|title=The Imperial Prize, Japan Academy Prize, Duke of Edinburgh Prize Recipients|publisher=Japan Academy|access-date=23 January 2010}}</ref>

==Books==
Kato has published several books in Japanese, of which some have already been translated into English. 

He wrote a book on [[Fermat's Last Theorem]] and is also the coauthor of two volumes of the trilogy on Number Theory, which have been translated into English.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.worldcat.org/search?q=kazuya+kato&dblist=638&fq=ap%3A%22kato+kazuya%22&qt=facet_ap%3A|title=Worldcat search|publisher=worldcat.org|access-date=23 January 2010}}</ref>
